item.title: A Tale of 3 Cormorants: Similar and Surprisingly Unique - Project Manaia
item.description: The Mediterranean is home to three birds in the family Phalacrocoracidae: the Pygmy Cormorant, European Shag and Great Cormorant.

item.title: Sailing for Science: My First Adventure with Project Manaia - Project Manaia
item.description: When I first applied for a scholarship to join Project Manaia, I was both excited and a little nervous. I had received a scholarship, which made the opportunity even more special. item.title: Porbeagles: A Shark of Distinction - Project Manaia
item.description: Porbeagles (Lamna nasus) are large, heavy bodied sharks which once proliferated in the Mediterranean and in many of the world’s oceans.

item.title: From Tunisia to Greece: My Scholarship Journey - Project Manaia
item.description: A Tunisian ecological engineering student joins Project Manaia for a marine research expedition in Greece with a marine biology scholarship, studying seagrass ecosystems and amphipods while gaining hands-on conservation experience at sea.

item.title: From Student to Group Leader: Volunteering in Marine Biology with Project Manaia - Project Manaia
item.description: At 18, I joined Project Manaia aboard Waya Waya in Italy. From sea turtle encounters to leading volunteers, here’s my marine biology journey at sea as a group leader.

item.title: A Prodigious Polychaete: The Vanadis Bristle Worm - Project Manaia
item.description: Just west of Naples, off the island of Ponza, lives one such species: the Vanadis bristle worm (Vanadis formosa).

item.title: The Sea Lizard: Synodus saurus - Project Manaia
item.description: Lizards are well known for their camouflage and quick, darting predatory attacks. Synodus saurus, commonly called the lizardfish, uses these same strategies.

item.title: Which biocide-free paint to choose for your boat? - Project Manaia
item.description: The discussions about the “best” antifouling paint are probably about as old as the boating industry itself - for sure, it is a conversation to be had in any marina every year. On board Waya Waya (and previously on Independence), we joined those discussions often and always ended up trying new things, such as biocide-free bottom paint.
